title: Antenatal screening timeline
summary: What's typically offered when across a straightforward pregnancy, as a quick memory-jogger.

blocks.heading: Booking (ideally by 10 weeks)
bullets: Full history and risk assessment, booking bloods, BMI, and early dating.

VERIFY the exact local booking bloods panel — commonly includes FBC, blood group and antibody screen, infectious disease screening, and haemoglobinopathy screening, but local policy sets the full list.

blocks.heading: Combined/dating scan (around 11–14 weeks)
bullets: Confirms dates and, if combined screening is chosen, measures nuchal translucency as part of screening for Down's, Edwards', and Patau's syndromes.

blocks.heading: Ongoing routine reviews
bullets: Blood pressure and urinalysis at every contact (pre-eclampsia screening).
Symphysis-fundal height measurement from around 24–28 weeks.
VERIFY the exact local appointment schedule, which varies by parity and risk factors.

blocks.heading: Around 24–28 weeks
bullets: Oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) offered if risk factors for gestational diabetes are present — VERIFY local risk-factor criteria and exact timing.
First dose of anti-D prophylaxis for Rhesus-negative women, per local protocol.

blocks.heading: Around 35–37 weeks
bullets: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) testing where this is offered locally — VERIFY local policy, as universal GBS screening is not standard practice across all of the UK.
